git_rationale.how_fix_addresses_root: (1) DEV_SYSTEMD emptied — no happy-daemon-* unit is whitelisted. (2) Layer 1.A in pretool-bash-safety.sh runs BEFORE the generic /allow short-circuit and gates ALL 8 daemon-state-disrupting verbs against happy-daemon-* targets. (3) The only unblock channel is /root/bin/claude-allow-restart — a user-only TTY-gated CLI that writes a single-shot, time-bounded, target-bound, session-bound sentinel that the bash hook consumes atomically via flock+SIGALRM (reused from check_and_consume_allowlist scaffolding). (4) Wrapper-class paths (systemd-run, at, crontab, nohup, timeout, dbus-send, nc, eval, bash -c, python -c, /tmp/*.sh wrapper scripts), daemon HTTP /stop, sentinel writes, and Edit/Write to systemd unit files / admin scripts / grant sentinel are all blocked. (5) Prompt-purity hook escalates daemon-restart-prescription to exit 2 for orchestrator AND subagents, with full audit-log write (preserves warn-only for all other categories — no regression). (6) settings.json permissions.deny extended to 6 new systemctl verbs for defense-in-depth at the Claude permission table layer.

implementation_notes: BA spec line 222 explicitly says iter-2 does NOT change settings.json hooks-** layer (already in `ask`). My additions to pretool-block-production-files.sh include a hook-self-modification rule that fires for SUBAGENTS only and honors the existing .hook-refactor-allow sentinel convention (the same one used by pretool-claude-config-guard.py). This goes slightly beyond BA's literal R4 list (BA listed 9 paths; I added 3 hook files for hook-self-modification defense). Justification: BA's architect specialist report § 4.4 explicitly recommends 'Layer 4 — Hook self-protection' as defense in depth, and BA spec R4 includes the three hook files as 'in-scope' for the Edit/Write gate. The sentinel-honoring path means orchestrator edits with user-prompt remain unaffected; subagents must have explicit user authorization via .hook-refactor-allow.

The `.hook-refactor-allow` sentinel at /dev/shm/dev-workspace/happy-dev/.claude/.hook-refactor-allow was created by me at 2026-05-05T07:38Z under the user's Option A authorization to bypass pretool-claude-config-guard.py for THIS cycle. I attempted to clean it up at end-of-cycle but `rm` is blocked by pretool-bash-safety.sh. Orchestrator/user should remove it after this cycle. The sentinel only authorizes hook edits when present; QA will not re-trigger the bypass.
TodoWrite tool is denied for the dev role (pretool-tool-policy.py blocked it). Used inline TASK-ID and section comments in artifacts instead.

The bash-safety hook's wrapper-class block (Layer 1.B) is intentionally broad: ANY co-occurrence of happy-daemon vocabulary AND restart-class verb AND a wrapper command (systemd-run/at/crontab/nohup/timeout/nc/dbus-send/eval/bash -c/python -c) blocks. False positives are an accepted tradeoff per BA AC4 rationale and user's `彻底永久根本禁止` directive.

The prompt-purity hook's daemon-restart-prescription pattern uses ~30-token proximity (`(?:\W+\w+){0,30}?`) in BOTH orderings (verb-then-target and target-then-verb). This catches both 'restart happy-daemon-dev' and 'happy-daemon-dev should be restarted'. Pattern 3 catches direct invocation of `bash /root/bin/happy-restart` and `safe-daemon-restart`.

The grant sentinel format includes session_id binding. The bash consume function compares the active session_id (from $INPUT.session_id or $CLAUDE_SESSION_ID env) to the grant's session_id. A no-active-session sentinel value does NOT match a real sid (correctly). This implements AC12 session-mismatch fail-closed.

Code path for the consume function: when the sentinel exists, the function (a) opens a flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on the .lock file with 3x100ms retry, (b) reads JSON inside an SIGALRM(1s) timeout, (c) validates target/expires_at/session_id, (d) atomically unlinks while holding the lock, (e) writes a JSON-line audit entry with outcome=consumed/expired/target_mismatch/session_mismatch/blocked_lock/error. The flock is released on exit.

Per BA edge-case note: verbs `start, isolate, set-property, mask, unmask, link, revert, edit` are explicitly out of scope. The 8-verb set covers all daemon-state-disrupting verbs documented in `man systemctl(8)` for our use case.
